Subject: Intro: Pinecone + Redwood - governance, fallback behavior & certification ask

Hi Rachel / Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the quick connect. I'm Sam on the Pinecone partnerships team — excited to explore a tighter integration with Redwood that helps customers use Pinecone as a primary vector store with S3 fallthrough for cold data. Two immediate things from our side:

1) Attached is a short SOC2/PCI summary we can share with prospects (pinecone-soc2-summary.pdf).
2) We can provision a sandbox project with index configs and sample payloads if you want to run perf/load tests.

Proposed agenda for an hour sync:
- Index configuration patterns (sparse vs dense, shard counts)
- S3 fallthrough semantics and caching TTLs
- Encryption & KMS handoff for customer-managed keys
- Failure modes and recommended fallback to local embeddings store
- Mutual action plan & deliverables (security artifacts, sandbox access, timeline)

Can you share 2-3 windows tomorrow for a 60m working session? I'll bring a short config pack and a couple of engineers.

Best,
Sam
Sam Choi
Partner Solutions, Pinecone

Thanks Sam — appreciate the summary and offer for a sandbox.

Quick context from our side (so the room is aligned): Redwood customers frequently expect a single API surface that can route reads/writes to multiple persistence backends (hosted Redwood store, third-party vector DBs, and S3 cold tier). For commercial and compliance reasons we need to validate:
- Data residency / region controls across vector stores and S3 fallthrough
- KMS/HSM integration points for customer-managed keys
- Recovery & snapshot semantics for backup/restore across index and S3 tiers
- Observable metrics (index size, query tail-latency, eviction rate)

Agenda proposal (60m):
1) Walk Pinecone index config + common failure scenarios (15m)
2) S3 fallthrough semantics & expected behavior under partial outage (15m)
3) Security artifacts we need to circulate (15m)
4) Next steps: MAP, sandbox creds, test data, and timeline (15m)

Attaching an RFC that sketches our integration expectations (RWD-pinecone-integration-RFC.pdf).

Availability: tomorrow 11:00-12:30 PT or 15:00-16:30 PT works for us. Marcus / Laura — is either window okay?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 10:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Attaching an RFC that sketches our integration expectations (RWD-pinecone-integration-RFC.pdf).

Thanks — quick technical checklist from my side to seed the call:
- Index snapshot semantics: how frequently can we request a full index export and what size delta snapshots do you support?
- S3 fallthrough strategy: expected TTLs for cache entries, cold object access latencies, and whether we can pin namespaces to S3-only for archival use cases.
- Routing & consistency: best-effort vs strong read-after-write guarantees for multi-backend routing.
- Encryption: support for customer-managed KMS keys and rotation windows; evidence we can log key usage to meet audit requirements.
- Observability: prometheus metrics and traces for query durations, cold-hit ratio, and evictions.
- Test assets: please provide sample index config (shards/replicas/vector dimension), and ~1GB of synthetic vectors we can use for perf testing in our sandbox.

If Pinecone can provide the sample config + vectors ahead of the call that would make the session much more actionable.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Choi <sam.choi@pinecone.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alexa Mehta <alexa@summitai.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: Pinecone + Redwood - governance, fallback behavior & certification ask

Thanks Marcus — good checklist. Answers inline and next steps below.

- Index snapshot semantics: We support full exports via our export API (payload gzipped). Incremental snapshots are available via change deltas for active writes; typical export cadence customers use is daily for warm indexes and weekly for cold archival. We'll attach representative index configs.
- S3 fallthrough: Our fallthrough is configurable per-index namespace. Cache TTLs are tunable; cold fetches to S3 from our tiered architecture are typically 50-300ms depending on object size and region. We can pin namespaces to S3-only if required for archival compliance.
- Routing & consistency: Pinecone provides read-after-write in the write primary region for 99.9% cases; cross-region eventual consistency applies for cross-region replication. We'll highlight caveats for multi-region failover.
- Encryption: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS + externally managed keys). Rotation can be scheduled; we will provide the KMS integration guide.
- Observability: We have a prometheus endpoint for metrics and a trace export (OTLP). We'll share the metric names and dashboards.

Attachments we are sharing now: pinecone-index-configs.yaml (example configs), and a small sample vector payload set for initial perf runs. We're provisioning a sandbox project and will share access by EOD. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-PineconeSandbox

Action items:
- Pinecone: Share sandbox creds + index config + sample vectors (EOD today)
- Redwood: Share MAP template and security questionnaire we need filled (Rachel to send)
- Both: Schedule a 60m working session during the 11:00-12:30 PT window tomorrow (Rachel to confirm)

We can also produce a short technical note on expected failure scenarios and suggested fallback logic for Redwood if you'd like us to draft that.

Best,
Sam
